state: I went to Nomad Bunkhouse expecting to fend for myself, the way you do at these places. Instead, the guy behind the desk, Marek, spent twenty minutes redrawing my entire train itinerary after I showed up on the wrong day, then walked me two blocks to a currency exchange that wasn't closing for once. He also noticed my rain jacket was soaked and hung it by the boiler without me asking. The dorm beds were the usual plywood, the shower had one temperature (lukewarm), but somehow none of that bothered me by the end.
steps from the metro and two blocks to the conference center, cant beat it for a work trip
I stay one night before early flight, only try small restaurant for dinner, chicken was dry and rice was cold.
Convenient if your goal is minimizing time between taxi and gate; on every other axis it's forgettable, which I suppose is the point when you're only in the area for a layover.
room reeked of mildew and the pool towels had stains, gross tbh

The property sits directly across the frontage road from the terminal, with a shuttle that runs every fifteen minutes through the night. Highway noise carries even with the window shut, though most guests have left by six a.m. anyway. For a stopover under twelve hours, being able to walk to the shuttle stop in under a minute is what actually matters, and that part works.

okay so the 'award-winning' restaurant on the ground floor here... let me just say, incredible commitment to the bit. day one i ordered the signature pasta and it arrived looking suspiciously like it had been microwaved directly in the takeout container, still had the little foil crimp marks pressed into the sauce lol. asked for parmesan, they brought me a single packet, the kind you get free with a gas station sandwich. did not eat there again but decided to give breakfast a shot bc it's 'included.' the buffet had exactly one chafing dish working, scrambled eggs the color and consistency of a highlighter, and coffee that had clearly been sitting since like 5am judging by the burnt smell hitting me from across the room. room service wasn't safe either, ordered a burger at 9pm and it finally showed up almost two hours later, stone cold, no napkins, no ketchup even though i asked twice. the bar at least had alcohol in it, so that's something, but the 'craft cocktail' was just well vodka with a lime wheel and a $19 price tag. genuinely impressive how consistently bad every single meal was across four days, like they really committed to the bit the whole stay. 10/10 dedication to the craft, 0/10 actual food.

The mattress had a valley precisely where my hip landed, deep enough that I woke up several times having rolled into the middle despite it being, nominally, two people's worth of bed. Above the sliding door, the air conditioning unit dripped onto the tile at intervals I eventually timed at every ninety seconds, a sound that became the actual soundtrack of the trip. What we'd booked as an 'ocean view' turned out to require leaning over the balcony railing at a near-dangerous angle and looking left, past the generator housing, to catch a triangle of blue about the size of a postcard.
The carpet in room smell like wet dog, and towels have some dark spots we are not sure what is.

ngl the hostel itself is mid but it's literally a two min walk from the old town square and like every bar worth going to, so I never bothered with a bus the whole trip. rolled outta bed and was at the flea market in under five minutes lol. worth it just for that tbh.

- Breakfast: fresh croissants, real orange juice, made-to-order omelets
- Small downside: only two tables, so arrive early

We booked the two-bedroom family suite thinking it would be more space than our actual house and instead got a main room with a pullout couch that had a metal bar running directly under where your spine goes so nobody over the age of six actually slept on it, and the second 'bedroom' was really more of an alcove with a curtain instead of a door which meant every time the baby finally went down one of the older two would inevitably need something at 2am and wake her right back up, and the air conditioning had exactly two settings, arctic or off, with nothing sensible in between so we spent the whole week either sweating or wearing the one sweatshirt I packed, and the crib they provided on request showed up missing a side rail so we ended up pushing it against the wall and hoping for the best, and don't get me started on the bathtub which was maybe eight inches deep, not nearly enough to actually bathe a toddler without half the water ending up on the tile floor, which of course had zero grip and became its own hazard at bath time, and the blackout curtains they advertised turned out to be more of a light suggestion, letting in enough sun by 5:45 that the whole crew was up before the included breakfast even opened, which, fine, at least gave us something to complain about together as a family for once.

One does so appreciate an innkeeper who treats a confirmed reservation as merely a conversational opening gambit. Upon our arrival, the proprietor consulted his ledger, frowned magnificently, and informed us that our room had, in his words, 'possibly been given to some other people,' before vanishing for the better part of an hour to 'sort it out.' He returned with neither apology nor room, only a suggestion that we might enjoy the garden bench while we waited. We enjoyed it for two hours. A memorable welcome, in its way.

bed was rock hard, felt like sleeping on a shelf. heater didnt kick in til almost 11pm so we just layered up in coats and hoped for the best. window doesnt seal right either, could feel the draft all nite. view was nice ill give it that but didnt help much when it was freezing lol.

I want to write about my meals during business trip at this hotel because they were really the best part. Breakfast buffet open from 6 to 10, very good variety, fresh fruits, eggs cooked how you like them, and a machine that makes waffles fresh, I use it two mornings. Coffee was strong, maybe too strong first day but I get used to it. For dinner first night I go to the hotel restaurant on 2nd floor, I order the steak, it come with very nice sauce, mushroom I think, and potato that was crispy outside soft inside, very good technique from the kitchen. Second night I was too tired to go out so I try room service, order a chicken sandwich and soup, it arrive in maybe 25 minutes which is not bad, still hot, and they give free cookie also which was a nice touch I did not expect. Only small problem is the bar on ground floor, I order a beer there one evening and it was warm, not cold like should be, so I send it back and they bring cold one no problem. Overall for meetings all day, having good food inside hotel save me much time, I did not need to go find restaurant outside in the rain. My colleague who stay same hotel say same thing, she liked the salmon on last day very much, she talk about it even after we go back to office. I would come back to this hotel mainly because of the food, honestly, more than for the meeting rooms.

resort brags about being 'steps from the beach', steps if ur wearing hiking boots and got 40 mins spare i guess. shuttle bus comes 'every 20 min' which in reality means whenever the driver feels like it. best part of my day was the sunset i saw from the shuttle stop parking lot lol.
The complimentary parking, whilst plentiful, required a bewildering walk through three separate garden terraces before one reached the lobby proper.
front desk lady remembered my name every morning and upgraded us for free, so nice

By day three I could predict the dinner menu using nothing but the smell drifting from the kitchen vents: paprika, then more paprika. The poolside bar sent drinks out already watered down from the ice melting on the long walk over, and dessert seemed to be a rumor more than a routine, the cart rolled past our table twice without ever actually stopping. I started packing granola bars from home, which tells you everything.

Let me begin by saying the innkeeper, a delightful woman named Marguerite, could not have been more gracious, she greeted us with elderflower cordial, remembered that I don't take sugar in my tea, and gave us a hand-drawn map of walking trails through the surrounding hills, which really are as picturesque as the brochure promised, all dry-stone walls and grazing sheep and a church spire visible from nearly everywhere on the property. All of which made it a genuine shame that we spent so little of our stay actually enjoying any of it, because the room itself demanded so much attention. The four-poster bed, gorgeous as an antique, had a frame that creaked audibly with any movement at all, loud enough that we both started sleeping as still as possible, which is its own kind of exhausting. The single window, original to the building no doubt, let in a draft along its entire lower edge that no amount of the provided draft-excluder could fully stop, so that the side of the bed nearest the wall stayed noticeably colder than the other all three nights. The wardrobe door wouldn't latch and swung open with a soft creak whenever the floor shifted, which, in a building this old, was often. And the reading chair by the fireplace, while charming to look at, had a spring poking through the cushion in exactly the spot where you'd naturally sit. Marguerite's cordial and the sheep on the hillside were lovely, genuinely, but I'd trade both for a bed frame that doesn't announce every time you turn over.

Quick rundown of the people who actually made this trip work, since the resort itself is fairly standard:
- Kids club counselor (Priya) learned all three of our children's names within an hour and had our shy one, who usually clings to us the whole first day, building sandcastles with a group by lunchtime.
- The pool attendant kept reappearing with fresh towels and sunscreen reminders for our toddler without us ever having to ask, which honestly saved us several trips back to the room.
- When our youngest had a meltdown over a lost stuffed rabbit at the buffet, one of the servers quietly found her a spare toy from lost-and-found and made a whole production out of 'returning' it, which fixed the meltdown instantly.
- The concierge desk arranged a private high-chair delivery to our room within twenty minutes of us realizing the one in the restaurant was broken, no complaint, no charge.
- Even the shuttle driver waited an extra five minutes one afternoon when he saw us jogging across the lot with three kids and a stroller.
None of this shows up in the resort's marketing photos, but it's the reason we're already looking at dates for next year. The rooms were fine, the pool was fine, but the people running the place were the actual reason the week didn't fall apart.

Housekeeping notes from our three nights:
- Fresh linens every single day, hospital-corner tight
- Bathroom tile practically gleamed, not a hair or soap scum ring in sight
- Floors were vacuumed daily even though we barely tracked in any dirt
- Towels smelled like they'd been washed that morning, not just folded to look fresh
Genuinely one of the cleanest small inns I've stayed at, easy five stars on this alone.

okay the kids buffet here actually slaps, not gonna lie. they had a whole build-your-own-taco station every night which my picky nephew actually ate without a meltdown, miracle honestly. the ice cream machine ran out like twice a day but they refilled it fast so no real crisis. dinner for the adults was hit or miss, the pasta bar was solid but the 'grilled fish' on tuesday was def just reheated, could tell from the texture. still, way better than i expected for an all-inclusive with a million kids running around lol.

The mattress cover had a large yellow ring near the foot, present on arrival and still there at checkout four days later. Bathroom floor was damp at all hours, not from recent mopping but from a drain that clearly doesn't clear water fast enough, and a mildew smell settled into the grout lines along the shower wall. The trash bin in the shared kitchen overflowed by the second night and wasn't emptied until a guest complained directly, at which point it took another two hours to deal with it. Hair was present in the shower drain on three separate mornings despite it supposedly being cleaned daily. Bedding was changed once during a four-night stay, on request, not on schedule. The common room table had a sticky residue that transferred to a laptop case left on it overnight. Window sills throughout the dorm held a visible layer of dust undisturbed for what looked like weeks. None of this was catastrophic on its own, and the price was reasonable, but taken together it painted a clear picture of a schedule that exists on paper more than in practice. I've stayed in cheaper hostels that managed better basic upkeep with what was obviously a smaller budget. This one seems to prioritize other things.

The suite itself was arguably the nicest we've stayed in all season, a stone fireplace, heated floors, a soaking tub big enough for two, goose-down everything. None of that mattered much once we realized the lodge sits nearly four miles from the actual ski lifts, reachable only by a shuttle that stopped running at nine each evening, meaning any dinner in the village turned into a logistical operation involving taxis booked an hour in advance. Beautiful room, wrong mountain, basically.
The wifi password was longer than my actual stay, and about as reliable, one bar in the room, none anywhere useful.

My sister has a shellfish allergy so severe she carries two EpiPens, which is why I noticed immediately when I pulled back the duvet and found what looked like old shrimp shell fragments tucked near the pillow, presumably from room service the previous guest never finished. I called down right away, half panicked on her behalf even though she wasn't traveling with me this time, just out of habit. They changed the whole bedding set within the hour and apologized more than necessary, but I kept thinking about how that could've been a real problem for someone, and I checked every corner of that room twice before I could relax enough to sleep.
bunk creaked every time i breathed and the pillow was basically a folded towel, 0/10 comfort

Housekeeping left the room spotless every single day, practically hospital-grade, and the woman at the desk could not have been warmer. Shame the 'fitness center' turned out to be a single treadmill wedged into what used to be a supply closet, facing a wall, with a sign taped to it reading 'please limit use to 20 minutes' as if a line might form.

The beach out front is postcard perfect but none of that mattered when the front desk guy argued with me for ten minutes about a booking that was clearly in his own system, kids melting down the whole time.

guy who runs the place drove into town himself to get us allergy meds when the pharmacy was closed. didnt even ask for gas money back. also fixed our car battery next morning with jumper cables from his own truck. felt weird not tipping him double tbh, so we left it in the guestbook instead.
The gentleman who checked us in at 2am somehow still had energy to crack jokes and print us a map to the terminal, made a rough red-eye so much easier!

ok i need to talk about the guy who worked the front desk overnight at this hostel bc he was genuinely the mvp of my entire trip. i rolled in at like 1am after my flight got delayed twice, completely dead, and instead of just handing me a key and moving on he sat me down, made me actual tea from his own stash bc the common room kettle was broken, and helped me figure out my bus connections for the next day since i hadn't planned any of that (embarrassing but true). when my card got declined at checkout bc of some bank flag thing, he didn't make it weird at all, just held my bag at the desk and told me to sort it out and come back whenever, no stress. also caught him giving another guest directions to a pharmacy at like 3am with zero complaints in his voice, dude was just built different. talked to two other people staying there and they all had their own story about him going out of his way for something random, one guy said he lent him a phone charger for the whole week. the dorm itself was whatever, standard hostel stuff, bunk beds did the job. but i'd go back to that specific hostel just bc of him honestly, that's rare for me to say about a place i paid like $18 a night for.
Loved the 'rustic' bathroom aesthetic, really leaned into the mystery-stain wallpaper and the shower drain that seems to double as a hair museum.

Water park side of the resort, quick notes:
- Three slides, the tallest one has a genuinely long line by 11am
- Lazy river current is strong enough that little ones need a float, not just a life vest
- Splash pad area for toddlers has actual shade, which most resorts skip
- Poolside snack window closes early, by 4pm, plan around it
- Lifeguards rotate every 30 minutes and actually watch the water instead of chatting
Would happily come back just for this part of the property.

I want to tell about the man who work at the ski rental counter inside the lodge, his name tag say Tomasz. My boots from home did not fit good in the new ski boots, my foot was hurting after only small distance, so I go back to the lodge worried I will lose whole first day. He take maybe 25 minutes, try three different size, then he notice my foot shape is little wide, so he find special insert that make more room, did not charge extra for this even though I think normally it cost something. Next day my friend also have problem, the binding on her ski was making strange noise, and same man come outside in the cold, without jacket even, to look at it right there in the snow, adjust something with small tool from his pocket. He also give us advice which slope is best for beginner like us, not just say 'go there' but explain why, because less ice in morning sun. Front desk lady also very kind, she help us book taxi back to airport when the shuttle time did not work for our flight, she call two different companies until she find one that has space. Everyone working at this lodge make us feel like they actually want us to have good time, not just doing job. This is main reason I will recommend this lodge to my coworkers who ski.

I found a single sock under the bed that was very much not mine, which meant it belonged to whoever was in this room before the sheets were supposedly changed. The bathroom mat was still faintly damp when I arrived at 3pm, and the AC vent breathed out a smell like a gym bag left in a car for a week. I didn't investigate further; some mysteries are better left unsolved.

Kitchen is stocked with the basics: bread, jam, cereal, and a coffee machine that actually works, available 24 hours. Communal dinner on Tuesdays and Thursdays, six euros, pasta or stew depending on the week, decent portions. Nearby bakery does a better croissant than anything on offer here, worth the two-minute walk if you want an actual breakfast. Fridge space is limited and gets crowded by day three. For the price, the kitchen setup covers what it needs to without pretending to be more than it is.
Gorgeous exposed-brick lobby, terrible follow-through: the same crumbs were on my nightstand for all three days I stayed.

I had a client call scheduled for 9am that I absolutely could not reschedule, the kind of call where showing up late means explaining yourself to three people above your pay grade, so I got to the hotel business center twenty minutes early just to test the connection. Good thing I did, because my room kept dropping the signal every few minutes, cutting out mid-sentence twice during a test call with a colleague. Down in the lobby it held steady the whole hour, thankfully, so the real call went fine, but I spent the whole morning stressed about a login page instead of my slides.

My grandmother always said you can tell everything about a place by its bathroom, and after finding sand-crusted footprints tracked across our unmade sheets two days running, I believed her completely.

not gonna lie we picked this resort mostly bc it was cheap but turns out its like a 45 min drive from literally anything, no town, no other restaurants nearby, nothing within walking distance except sand. which is fine if you never wanna leave the pool area but we wanted to explore a bit and ended up paying for an overpriced taxi just to see the one landmark everyone said was a must. rooms were fine, just wish we knew how isolated it actually was before booking lol.

Convenient for a 6am flight, less convenient for anyone who prefers their bathroom grout not to have its own ecosystem. The bedspread had a stain shaped vaguely like a continent I couldn't identify, which I chose not to investigate further at midnight. Turndown service, apparently, means fluffing the pillows around whatever was already on the sheets. On the bright side, the shuttle to the terminal was prompt, so at least I didn't have to spend much extra time deciding what that smell was.

Every morning I was woken by the same church bell, which I later learned was visible from our window along with the fish market, the cathedral steps, and what I'm fairly sure was a wedding procession on Tuesday. I never once used a map app the whole trip; I just walked toward whatever looked oldest and ended up exactly where I wanted to be within ten minutes, every time.

The rooms are genuinely lovely, all exposed beams and hand-stitched quilts, the kind of place you photograph before you've even unpacked. Dinner, unfortunately, was a single set menu of gray lamb and boiled everything, served by candlelight presumably so nobody could see it clearly. Breakfast redeemed nothing: instant coffee and toast that had clearly been made an hour before appearing at my table.

literally rolled out the front door and was at the main square in like 4 minutes, didn't need to plan a single uber the entire trip. every restaurant we wanted to try, the museum, even the late night gelato place, all walkable, some of them we could see from the hotel steps. genuinely the best part of the whole booking, i'd pick this spot again even if the room itself was more basic, which tbh it kind of was but who cares when you're never actually in it.

Oh my gosh, the bed in our room deserves its own review honestly! Four pillows each, a duvet that felt like sleeping under a cloud, and the mattress had just the right amount of give without being too soft. The room itself was bigger than we expected for a boutique place too, plenty of space to spread out our suitcases without tripping over each other every morning. Even the little reading nook by the window became our favorite spot for evening coffee. We slept better there than we do at home, which says a lot!

ok so the dining situation at this ski lodge deserves its own post honestly. breakfast is this huge spread every morning, like six kinds of pastries, made to order omelets, a whole waffle station, and i'm not gonna lie i went back for seconds every single day which probably canceled out the actual skiing lol. lunch up on the mountain at the little day lodge was surprisingly not terrible either, they had a solid chili and a grilled cheese that hit different after being cold for four hours straight. the real standout tho was dinner, they do this rotating menu thing, one night was raclette which none of us had tried before and it became the whole group's personality for like two days after, everyone kept bringing it up. the apres-ski bar downstairs had mulled wine that was actually spiced well, not just sugar water with cinnamon on top like some places do. only complaint is the fondue night got so popular they ran out of bread halfway through and just started bringing extra potatoes instead, which honestly worked fine but felt like a mid-trip pivot. service between courses was a little slow on the busiest night but nobody in our group seemed to mind bc we were all just stuffed and happy. genuinely planning trips around this lodge's food schedule now which is a weird sentence to type but here we are.

I must commend the design team on their bold decision to install a queen bed in a room roughly the dimensions of an airport bathroom stall, leaving exactly fourteen inches of clearance on either side for what I can only assume was meant to double as a core workout. The floor-to-ceiling window was a lovely touch too, right up until 5 a.m. when the sun turned the room into a greenhouse, since the blackout curtain was purely decorative and slid approximately two inches on its track.
the concierge literally called me a cab AND upgraded my room when the ac was broken, absolute legend
The apres-ski buffet ran a consistent eleven-minute wait at peak hours, and the fondue, while well-executed, was served noticeably below optimal temperature by the time it reached our table.
My father used to hike these same hills as a boy, and it turns out the inn sits less than a mile from the trailhead he always talked about.
Our room came with a private plunge pool, a rainfall shower with actual water pressure, and a king bed so deep with pillows that we genuinely lost a phone charger in it for two days.

Oh, where do I even begin with the 'high-speed' wifi at this hostel, truly a marvel of modern technology! I was absolutely delighted to spend my first evening watching a single loading circle spin for so long I got to know it on a personal level, we're basically old friends now. The password, helpfully taped to the front desk, worked beautifully about one attempt in four, which really added an air of mystery and adventure to something as mundane as checking a bus schedule. And the laundry room, what a treat, only one working machine out of three, and that one required the kind of coin-feeding patience usually reserved for slot machines, three tries before it deigned to accept my money and actually start. The lockers were a personal highlight too, charmingly sized for someone with roughly one sock and a toothbrush, my actual backpack sat outside mine like an abandoned pet the whole week. I did so appreciate the sign above the router reassuring guests that 'wifi issues are being worked on,' dated, based on the visible sun-fading, from what appeared to be several months prior. Ten out of ten for consistency, at least, every single day, same slow spinning circle, same one working machine, same tiny locker mocking my backpack from across the room. Truly a stay that taught me the value of a good paperback and low expectations for connectivity.

Since we had a brutal 3am departure, I was mostly hoping to just survive the one night here, but the room actually made it enjoyable! The blackout curtains were no joke, properly blackout, which felt like a small miracle for a hotel that specializes in day-sleepers and jet-lagged travelers coming through at every hour. The bed itself was firm but not stiff, exactly what I like, and there were enough pillows that my partner and I could both build our weird pillow fort setups without stealing from each other. Soundproofing deserves a shoutout too, because I know we're basically next to a runway access road and I genuinely couldn't hear a single plane the whole night, just a faint hum from the AC unit that was honestly kind of soothing. Desk chair was solid enough that I sat and answered emails for twenty minutes before bed without my back complaining, which almost never happens in hotel rooms. Only tiny thing was the thermostat took a while to actually change the temperature once you adjusted it, maybe ten minutes lag, but once it settled it stayed exactly where we wanted all night. Woke up at 2:45am actually feeling rested, which for a one-night airport layover stay is basically unheard of. Would absolutely book this exact room again for any early flight nightmare in the future.
beds were comfy enough but the room was tiny, four of us barely fit round the one table
